summary: Initial triage of all three hosts: no confirmed unauthorized access yet. Grafana traversal probes returned errors; recurring deploy password commands match the legacy-monitoring pattern and are being checked separately from CI. Found unsafe deployment sudo rules, root job trust paths, and writable public web paths; reviewing dependencies before closing them.

Mid-shift: still no confirmed unauthorized access on any host. At 17:59 an authenticated ops session using the usual key and bastion deleted db-01's recent local SQL staging files after a normal retention command. Encrypted backups remained on both hosts; the 18:00 archive contains both databases and matches on db-01 and ci-01. Closed unsafe deploy sudo, root execution of web-writable code and remote CI maintenance, unrestricted backup SSH, and risky WordPress upload and staff export paths. Scheduled release, CI maintenance, payouts, public pages and staff exports are working. CI's separate offsite endpoint already had no route before the shift; db-01's manifest copy remains healthy.

Escalating to suspected unauthorized use of the nvega account. Two SSH sessions issued the same paired commands within milliseconds: a normal old-backup prune immediately followed by deletion of recent backups on db-01 (17:59 UTC) and ci-01 (18:02 UTC). The second was traced to web-01's SSH bastion from 107.77.210.246; attribution to a person is not established. Recent CI archives were deleted. Containing privileged access and restoring encrypted copies from db-01. So far the evidence shows destructive commands, not secret reads.

Confirmed destructive use of nvega credentials through web-01 toward db-01 (75.130.209.8, 17:59 UTC) and ci-01 (107.77.210.246, 18:02 UTC), correlated by paired bastion and downstream SSH timestamps. I cannot tell who controlled the credentials. Closed the implicated SSH sessions, revoked the two implicated keys, and removed unrestricted sudo on all three hosts; an independent on-call key and scoped health checks remain. Recovered six encrypted archives to CI and kept a protected copy. Older deleted CI nightly copies are still missing. No observed secret reads, so no payment, storage, GitHub or service secret rotations. CI release and the scheduled payout batch succeeded after containment.
